get.summary: The project's History: steps newest first (stepId, parentStepId, display sequence, label, summary — what changed, in user terms, or null — author, startedAt, endedAt — its close, or its last change while open — isOpen while its request or Background run runs, note — "part 2", "212 of 340 paragraphs, cancelled", "interrupted", without brackets — or null, kind — request | backgroundRun | restore | started | import, action — what a request's or Background run's step does: edit | editWithAi | insert | split | merge | delete | title | pause | character | voice | attribution, null on the other kinds — restoredFromStepId — the step a Restore brought back, else null — and cantOpen), headStepId (the tip; null before the first step), busy ({ reason } while anything is queued or running for the project, else null) and restoring (a Restore of the project is running). One History step, in the shape GET /history lists it, plus restorePreview: { audioDiscardCount } — how many items would lose their audio if the project were restored to it now (their text, speaker or delivery cue differs there, or the step doesn't have them) — or null for a step that can't be opened. 404 unknown project or step; 409 while anything is queued or running for the project, or it is restoring (detail says what), since a busy project can't be viewed at a step; 503 when opening the step failed for a reason that passes (try again).

post.summary: Restore: make the project as it stood after the step current, as a new step ("Restore to 'Split chapter' (14:02)", restoredFromStepId set) — every later step stays in History. Records keep their ids; items whose text, speaker or delivery cue changes lose their audio and its review, items brought back return without audio, the Pipeline checkpoints it disturbs go stale, and voices, voice reference audio, the cover and the source file come back too; app-wide LLM and TTS settings are untouched. Open Edit with AI sessions for the project are dropped. Answers { step, audioDiscardCount, needsAudioCount } — needsAudioCount is the items without audio after it, the brought-back ones included; step is null when the project already was that state. While it runs every other write and enqueue for the project is 409 "Project is restoring". 404 unknown project or step; 409 while anything is queued or running for the project, or it is already restoring (detail says why); 422 a step that can't be opened; 503 when opening it failed for a reason that passes (try again).

post.summary: Add a Pronunciation { writtenForm, spokenForm }. Both are trimmed and inner whitespace collapsed to one space. Written form: 1–100 characters, starting and ending with a letter or digit; spoken form: 1–200 characters. 201 with the entry, its reach and what it cost; 400 invalid; 409 when another entry has the written form, ignoring case. One History step, labelled Pronunciation: add "<written>". Items with audio whose Spoken text the change alters lose it (WAV reference and audio review), as a text edit does; audioDiscardCount counts them, needsAudioCount the spoken items without audio after it. 409 while audio generation is queued or running for the project, or a Restore runs. An X-Origin-Id header (GUID) is echoed as originId on the mutation receipt the live hub publishes.

What saving a draft { id?, writtenForm, spokenForm, delete? } would do, writing nothing: no id adds, an id edits that entry, delete: true deletes it (forms ignored). Answers matchCount, itemCount, withAudioCount (a delete's: the entry's reach now), audioDiscardCount (exactly what the save would discard), overlaps (entries whose written form holds the draft's as whole words or is held by it, draftWins when the draft's is the longer and so wins), duplicateOf (another entry with the written form, ignoring case: a save would be 409; the counts treat the draft as taking its place), and matches in book order: itemId, chapterId, chapterTitle, speaker, hasAudio, the sentence around it, sentenceStart (where it starts in the item's text, what a try-out names it by), matchStart and matchLength in that sentence, spokenSentence, the sentence with the drafted list applied, and spokenMatchStart and spokenMatchLength, where the match's spoken form (its case carried over) sits in spokenSentence. 400 invalid; 404 unknown id.

Unknown chapters match nothing.

post.summary: Render one try-out sentence { itemId, sentenceStart, draft?, asWritten, voice }: the sentence of the item starting at sentenceStart (an impact match's), carried on over a match that runs past its end. Answers the WAV body (audio/wav); nothing is stored and no item's audio changes. 400 invalid draft, no sentence starts there or a bad voice; 404 unknown item, voice or entry; 409 while attribution, audio generation or a voice batch is queued or running anywhere (it holds the GPU); 422 no voice resolves, the voice has no audio or no TTS config is active; 503 TTS busy or down.

An X-Origin-Id header (GUID) is echoed as originId on the mutation receipt the live hub publishes.

put.summary: Edit a Pronunciation's { writtenForm, spokenForm }, checked as an add. 200 with the entry, its reach and what it cost; 400 invalid; 404 unknown id; 409 when another entry has the written form. Items with audio whose Spoken text the change alters lose it (WAV reference and audio review), as a text edit does; audioDiscardCount counts them, needsAudioCount the spoken items without audio after it. 409 while audio generation is queued or running for the project, or a Restore runs. get.summary: The Setup check report: one row per check (id, group, name, tier, result, expected, found, note?, fix { text, link?, copy? }), the times of the last Quick and Full check, firstRun (this start created app.db), putBack (after a Full check, what it did with the containers it drove), startedAt (when this host started) and noWorkspace (this host started without a usable Workspace: every other API call answers 503 No Workspace until the app restarts). Empty rows until the start-up Quick check ends.

post.summary: Re-run one Full-tier check (a row whose rerun isn't null) in the background: only the steps that judge it (similarity transcribes first, to score a real transcript), under the Full check's rules — queues wait, Preflight refuses new AI tasks, the containers it drives are put back, and progress goes out as setupCheck messages. rerun.gpu says it stops the running GPU container. The report's fullCheckedAt stays the last whole Full check's. 202 with the report (fullRun shows the re-run); 404 for an unknown or Quick-tier id; 409 while a Full check runs, while work is in flight (named, as for the Full check), before the start-up Quick check ends, when the check has no active config, or when its rerun.gpu is stale (the check now drives a GPU container: run the Quick check first).

Start the Full check in the background, or join the Full check already going (one per host): 202 with the report, whose fullRun { step, total, lane: local|cpu|gpu, label, cancelling } shows the run. While it runs every queue waits and Preflight refuses new AI tasks with "Setup check running". Progress and the final report go to every live hub client as setupCheck { kind: progress|done, report }. 409 naming the work in flight while the Audio or Character queue holds items, or a voice batch, discovery or assembly runs, and while one check re-runs.
Cancel the Full check: it stops once the current step ends, and the checks it hadn't reached read Not run. 202 with the report (fullRun.cancelling true); 409 when none is running.

Run the Quick check (Workspace, ffmpeg, docker CLI) and answer the new report. It never starts, stops or switches anything; it creates the Workspace folder when missing. While a Full check runs it answers the run's report instead.
Cancel the running voice batch. 204, also when none is running.
